questions.prompt: A map traces ghettos, deportation routes, killing centers, occupied territories, and rail networks. What is the most responsible interpretation?
choices: Infrastructure and occupation made mass deportation and murder logistically possible, while documentary evidence is still required to establish policy, intent, responsibility, and local variation.
Rail proximity alone caused the Holocaust.
Every occupied territory experienced identical policies at the same time.
A transport map is sufficient to explain perpetrators' motives.
questions.explanation: Spatial logistics are crucial evidence, but genocide analysis also requires documentary evidence about intent, policy, institutions, perpetrators, victims, and local conditions.
